filters out own frontend_id from "others"; setActiveUsers([myUser, ...others]), setCollaboratorCount
if plan_id in room_states: send {'{'}type:"SYNC_STATE", state: room_states[plan_id]{'}'} — late joiner catches up

User drops on target day/index → DndContext onDragEnd(event)
manager.broadcast(plan_id, data, sender=ws) — fan-out to room

6. Remote Clients Apply State — itineraryStore syncs, UI re-renders
from re-triggering its own subscribe() broadcast
days[], selectedPlaces, totals recompute → itinerary board re-renders (drag-drop columns, day cards, cost totals) with the new order
WebSocketDisconnect raised (tab close, network drop, unmount cleanup: ws.close())
if room empty → delete room entirely
if users remain → broadcast updated {'{'}type:"PRESENCE", users{'}'}
• Room capacity: ConnectionManager.MAX_COLLABORATORS = 15 — the 16th connect attempt gets {'{'}type:"ERROR", message:"Room is full (max 15)"{'}'} then the socket is closed.
• Server holds NO persistent DB state for room contents — room_states is an in-memory dict keyed by plan_id, lost on server restart; it exists purely to hydrate late joiners.
• broadcast() always excludes the sender (sender=websocket param) — the origin client never receives its own SYNC_STATE/DRAG_START/DRAG_END echoed back.
• Echo-loop prevention is client-side: isRemoteUpdate.current flag + 100ms setTimeout window blocks the subscribe() callback from re-broadcasting a just-applied remote SYNC_STATE.
• DRAG_START/DRAG_END are ephemeral presence signals (who is dragging what) — they do NOT mutate itineraryStore directly; only SYNC_STATE payloads call useItineraryStore.setState().
• JOIN messages carry a client-generated frontend_id (persisted across reconnects) plus a randomly assigned "Anonymous <Animal>" display name and color for anonymous collaborators.

• A guest opening a shared link with an empty local trip store is protected: itinerary.initializeDays() is skipped if syncReceived.current is true, so SYNC_STATE isn't clobbered by a blank local init.
• send_json calls to dead sockets are wrapped in try/except: pass — a stale connection is silently ignored rather than crashing the broadcast loop for other members.
• dev vs prod WS host resolution: ws://localhost:8002/api/ws/plan/{'{'}id{'}'} in NODE_ENV=development, else NEXT_PUBLIC_WS_URL (Render backend) or same-origin wss:// fallback.
Message type summary (as literally sent over the socket)
JOIN {'{'} user: {'{'} frontend_id, name, color, picture {'}'} {'}'} — sent on connect, and again whenever local user identity changes
PRESENCE {'{'} users: [...] {'}'} — server-computed roster, sent after JOIN and after disconnect
SYNC_STATE {'{'} state: <full itineraryStore snapshot> {'}'} — sent on every non-remote store mutation; cached server-side per room
DRAG_START / DRAG_END {'{'} placeId, userId (server-injected) {'}'} — ephemeral, drives the "being dragged by ..." UI badge only
ERROR {'{'} message: "Room is full (max 15)" {'}'} — sent once, immediately followed by websocket.close()
